title: tools: Start migrating checkAPIs.pl to Python
description:
Add check_apis.py, which is an initial, minimally tested AI translation.

Change count_errors to Boolean values.

AI-Assisted: yes [Claude Opus 4.6]

notes.body: restored source branch `checkapi-python`
marked this merge request as **draft**
Marking as a draft for now, since I've only made a light pass through the code.
changed the description

added 1 commit
  • 2c03a0f0 - tools: Start migrating checkAPIs.pl to Python
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/24826/diffs?diff_id=1790982378&start_sha=e1e83519e70e1eead3bcb22f45528e43e592bddc)

I should have done this long ago - mostly I didn't want to learn enough perl to understand exactly what it was doing.  There is some overlap with checks that check_typed_item_calls.py does, I will try to have a good look this weekend.

I also had the idea to do this after having to make a change to checkAPIs.pl yesterday.  Glad I checked the MR list first.
But I want to ask the question of "expanded scope" - Should we do this with all of the perl tool scripts? (as separate MRs, obviously)
Not answering for Gerald, but I believe that we would ideally like to completely lose the dependency on perl.
I would like that too. Some of the dissector regeneration scripts might be a long way off replacing, though.

> Should we do this with all of the perl tool scripts?

I think so. There's nothing wrong with Perl per se, but as our Python check script collection grows, the Perl scripts seem to be more and more out of place, and we recommend against installing Strawberry Perl in the Developer's Guide.
So are some developers not running current checkAPIs.pl because they don't have perl installed at all (and are relying on the pipeline to catch those errors)?
**grep perl tools/\*.sh** shows that for most platforms, perl will be installed without any much effort.
I'm assuming that the big outlier here is Windows. Perl ships with macOS and is usually present on most Linux and BSD systems.
This could logically be a set, but I think all we do is iterate over it.
Done.
I would look to have it use some of the functions in check_common.py (finding list of files from list, folder, git history).

I don't remember seeing ett\_ warnings trigger from the perl script.  check_typed_item_calls.py can detect declared-but-not-registered (only if they are registered using a literal array - if added element-by-element it doesn't match).

The perl script does find some things in this area that I don't check in check_typed_item_calls.py, but it doesn't:

* check them against calls to those items
* substitute simple macros (or easily-parsed enums) into places like the bitmask

I would argue that this is best done in one place, though currently check_typed_item_calls.py doesn't run from the commit hook.
Probably wouldn't be a bad idea to look at all of the scripts as a whole and see if "refactoring" can be done
There is a version of this in check_common.py, if there are better things about this one, I would like to merge them into there.
left review comments

The python version finds some warnings that the perl version did not.  It does take 20 times as long to run though!

We run run it through -m cProfile and likely speed it up.

Probably this script won't often be run across all of the dissectors, but the other thing I did with the other scripts was to use concurrent.futures.ProcessPoolExecutor() to get a \> 10x speedup (when running on my laptop).
mentioned in merge request !24828

Virtually all of the time is spent in re.findall() need to find out which one(s) are slow and see what may be done.

![image.png](/uploads/1220151269918c37bcc2cf99650b317a/image.png){width=495 height=138}
The re in `find_api_in_file` is very slow. I added a simple `api in file_contents` check and it sped things up considerably.
The performance is much closer now (30s for perl, 40s for python).

Blank line removal was broken in both scripts. I couldn't figure out how to fix it in checkAPIs.pl but I fixed it in check_apis.py. Quoted string removal was broken in check_apis.pl; that's been fixed as well. It looks like Claude Opus has trouble with complex regexes.

When I run check_apis.py on *epan/dissectors/packet-\*.c* I get

```
Error: epan/dissectors/packet-scsi-mmc.c uses proto_tree_add_uint with tvb_get_*. Use proto_tree_add_item instead
	Args: tree, hf_scsi_mmc_track, try_tvb, 2, 1, tvb_get_uint8(try_tvb, try_offset + 2)
Error: epan/dissectors/packet-scsi-mmc.c uses proto_tree_add_uint with tvb_get_*. Use proto_tree_add_item instead
	Args: tree, hf_scsi_mmc_session, try_tvb, 3, 1, tvb_get_uint8(try_tvb, try_offset + 3)
```
I saw those, that TRY_SCSI_CDB_ALLOC_LEN macro makes my head itchy.  try_offset appears to be 0, so the suggested changes should be ok, but I can't help thinking I'm missing something...
Same here. Either way it looks like the check_apis.py complaint is correct in this case.

I would be happy for this to be merged now/soon, and for me over the next few days to:

* have it use check_common.py functions
* compare/reduce some overlapping functionality with check_typed_item_calls.py, and decide whether both should be called in the pipeline, or whether some safe/reliable checks should be moved/consolidated to here
